results.result: The authors describe the challenges of gene editing in Leishmania, including a repetitive genome, limited DNA repair mechanisms, lack of RNA interference in most species, and limitations of existing CRISPR and bar-seq approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C26-C36, and C119-C126 collectively establish the biological and technical challenges that motivate the study. These are well-supported by citations to prior work and represent established knowledge in the field. The claims are consistent and provide appropriate context for the improvements presented.

results.result: The authors previously developed a CBE system for Leishmania (Engstler and Beneke, 2023) that had several limitations including low transfection efficiency (~1/30,000 cells), variable editing rates across species, growth defects, and competition between deleterious and non-deleterious mutations.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C8 and C37-C47 describe the prior CBE system and its limitations, all supported by citation to Engstler and Beneke, 2023. These claims establish the baseline for comparison and are internally consistent. The limitations are clearly stated and provide justification for the improvements presented in the current work.

results.result: A T7 RNAP promoter variant (T7 T10 GG) was identified that enables high editing rates without compromising parasite growth, achieving complete tdTomato knockdown in 7 days compared to 33 days with the previous system.
results.evaluation: Claims C9 and C48-C54 describe the optimization of the T7 RNAP promoter, supported by data in Figure 1. The comparison shows clear improvement (7 vs 33 days for complete knockdown) with no significant growth defects (doubling times 7.5-8.1 hr). The data are quantitative and include appropriate controls comparing multiple promoter variants.

results.result: AsCas12a ultra-mediated DSBs increase donor DNA integration efficiency regardless of homology flank length, with Cas12a crRNA-4 achieving the highest efficiency (~1 transfectant per 2,300 cells) and enabling accurate integration with homology flanks as short as 30 nt.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C69 describe the Cas12a integration system, supported by data in Figure 2. The results show ~25-fold improvement with Cas12a crRNA, independence from homology flank length (600, 60, 30 nt tested), and Sanger sequencing confirmation of flawless integration. The variation in crRNA efficiency (500-fold difference between crRNA-3 and crRNA-4) is documented with quantitative data.

results.result: Integration of CBE sgRNA expression cassettes into the 18S rRNA SSU locus using Cas12a crRNA-4 achieves complete tdTomato depletion in 7 days across all tested species, with transfection efficiency reaching 1 transfectant per 70 cells using Lonza Nucleofector technology—a ~400-fold improvement over the previous method.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C70-C78 describe the combined CBE-Cas12a system, supported by data in Figure 3. The 400-fold improvement in transfection efficiency is quantitatively documented (from 1/30,000 to 1/70 cells). Complete tdTomato depletion in 7 days is shown across L. donovani, L. mexicana, and L. major. The claim about library representation (C77) is a calculation based on achieved efficiency and is reasonable.

results.result: The improved system achieves rapid and complete editing of PF16 (6 days post-transfection) with paralysis phenotype in L. mexicana and L. donovani, confirmed by Illumina sequencing showing 100% editing with 35× genome coverage.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C87 describe PF16 targeting experiments, supported by data in Figures 4 and 4—figure supplement 1. The rapid editing (6 days) and complete mutation are documented by both motility analysis and Illumina sequencing. The reversal in one L. mexicana line (C84) is noted and explained by growth defect (C85), which is appropriately discussed as a limitation.

results.result: ONT and Illumina sequencing confirm that CBE sgRNA cassettes integrate as single copies on separate alleles in L. mexicana, with only one guide per transfectant, while L. donovani and L. major show some integration of multiple guides (2/10 clones).
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C92, C94-C96 describe integration patterns, supported by ONT/Illumina sequencing (Figure 4—figure supplements 1-3). The single-copy integration in L. mexicana is well-documented by read coverage analysis and ONT mapping. The species difference (multiple guides in 2/10 L. donovani and L. major clones) is clearly stated and represents an improvement over the previous system where 1/3 had multiple plasmids (C93).

results.result: A small-scale pooled screen successfully confirmed essential and fitness-associated functions of CK1.2, CRK2, CRK3, AUK1/AIRK, TOR1, IFT88, IFT139, IFT140, and RAB5A in L. mexicana, with 10-20× stronger depletion ratios and reduced error margins compared to the previous method.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C22 and C97-C112 describe the pooled screen results, supported by data in Figure 5. The screen design is appropriate (24 targeting sgRNAs, 15 non-targeting controls, ~25,000 cells/sgRNA representation). Strong depletion of targeting sgRNAs vs stable non-targeting controls is shown, with most sgRNAs falling outside the 99% confidence interval. The comparison to method v1 (C112) shows clear quantitative improvement. A few sgRNAs showed no depletion (C109), which is appropriately noted.

results.result: A revised CBE sgRNA scoring system was developed that prioritizes STOP codon generation by calculating the ratio of available cytosines to resulting STOP codons and considering STOP codon position within the editing window.
results.evaluation: Claims C10, C113-C114 describe the improved scoring system shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4. While the scoring system is clearly described and implemented (available at leishbaseedit.net), the manuscript states it 'will be systematically tested in future studies.' Without validation data showing improved performance, the actual utility of this scoring system remains uncertain.

results.result: Co-expression of AsCas12a ultra, T7 RNAP, and CBE enables hybrid CRISPR gene replacement and base editing, demonstrated by successful PF16 knockout using Cas12a-mediated gene replacement with 30 nt homology flanks.
results.evaluation: Claims C23, C115-C118 describe the hybrid approach, supported by data in Figure 6. The successful gene replacement is confirmed by PCR, Sanger sequencing of integration sites, and motility phenotype analysis. This demonstrates the versatility of the system, though it represents a proof-of-concept rather than extensive validation.

results.result: The triple-expression construct increased transfection efficiency by ~400-fold to 1 transfectant per 70 transfected cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C12 is the key quantitative result for transfection efficiency improvement, supported by data in Figure 3C. The 400-fold improvement is calculated from the previous rate of 1/30,000 (C46) to the new rate of 1/70 cells, achieved using Lonza Nucleofector technology with 1×10^8 cells and 10 µg DNA. This is a major technical achievement that enables large-scale screens.

results.result: These improvements will broaden the range of possible gene editing applications in Leishmania species and enable genome-wide CBE screens in the near future.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C25, C129 represent forward-looking statements about the impact of the work. While speculative, they are reasonable given the demonstrated improvements: 400-fold increase in transfection efficiency, ability to achieve 500-fold library representation with 20×10^8 cells, successful proof-of-concept pooled screen, and the statement that genome-wide screens with 40,000 sgRNAs have been completed (mentioned in Results).

results.result: The dual-construct system requires generation of a stable cell line first but offers the advantage of efficient CBE sgRNA integration using AsCas12a-mediated DSBs.
results.evaluation: Claims C127-C128 provide a balanced assessment of the dual-construct system's trade-offs. The disadvantage (requiring stable cell line generation) and advantage (efficient integration) are both clearly demonstrated in the manuscript. This represents an honest evaluation of the method's limitations and benefits.

results.result: The authors identified a T7 RNAP promoter variant (T7 T10 GG or T7 G10 GG) that ensures high editing rates across Leishmania species without compromising parasite growth. Using a dual-construct system, complete knockdown of the tdTomato reporter was achieved with all T7 RNAP promoter variants, while the unmodified T7 promoter caused an almost twofold increase in doubling time. The modified promoters (T7 T10 GG, T7 G10 GG) resulted in no significant growth rate increase, with doubling times ranging from 7.5 to 8.1 hr, and complete tdTomato depletion was achieved in just 7 days compared to 33 days previously.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, with one stating 'Fig.1 clearly describes reduced impairment in growth of parasites expressing sgRNAs via changes in promoters' and another noting the authors 'significantly reduce the non-specific toxicity of sgRNA expression whilst retaining high editing efficiencies.' The editor describes this as part of a 'meticulously-developed improved strategy' with 'reduced background toxicity.'

results.result: The authors created a triple-expression construct for stable integration of CBE sgRNA expression cassettes into the 18S rRNA SSU locus using AsCas12a ultra-mediated DNA double-strand breaks. This approach increased transfection efficiency by ~400-fold to 1 transfectant per 70 transfected cells. Cas12a-induced DSBs increased the rate of correct donor DNA integration irrespective of homology flank length, with Cas12a crRNA-4 performing significantly better than other crRNAs. High transfection efficiencies were reached, yielding up to one transfectant out of ~470 transfected parasites, with the Lonza Nucleofector technology boosting efficiency by an additional 20-fold.
results.evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this finding, with one noting 'Figs.2 and 3 compellingly document the usefulness of using AsCas12a for integration after transformation' and another stating the authors 'increase the transfection efficiency 400-fold.' A reviewer explicitly confirms 'The cell editing frequency of 1 edit per 70 cells reported in this study represents a 400-fold improvement over the previously published protocol.'

results.result: Using the improved system, complete depletion of the tdTomato signal was observed just 7 days post transfection in all tested species when integrating CBE sgRNA expression cassettes into the 18S rRNA SSU locus. The expression of CBE, T7 RNAP, AsCas12a ultra, and the CBE sgRNA had minimal or no impact on parasite growth across all three species. In L. major, the homo-polymer was fully introduced in 14 days using the T7 RNAP promoter-based dual vector system, while no editing was observed with the ribosomal promoter system. Just 6 days post transfection, the PF16 target site was fully edited and the overwhelming majority of cells were paralyzed. Illumina and ONT sequencing confirmed that cassettes integrated on separate alleles with only one CBE sgRNA cassette copy per L. mexicana cell.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm these findings, with one stating 'Figs.1 and 4 demonstrate the capacity of the combined modifications to efficiently edit a gene in three different Leishmania species.' The editor describes the work as 'meticulously-developed' with 'enhanced efficiency relative to a previously-described method.' No concerns are raised about the editing efficiency or integration data.

results.result: Using the improved system for a small-scale proof-of-principle pooled screen, the authors successfully confirmed the essential and fitness-associated functions of CK1.2, CRK2, CRK3, AUK1/AIRK, TOR1, IFT88, IFT139, IFT140, and RAB5A in Leishmania mexicana. sgRNAs targeting essential and fitness-associated genes were strongly depleted, while non-targeting control sgRNAs remained unchanged. Only two IFT88, two CRK3, and one CRK2 sgRNAs showed no reduction in abundance. The comparison between method v1 and v2 revealed significant improvements, with the new method achieving ~10–20× stronger ratios with substantially reduced error margins for the non-targeting controls.
results.evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this finding, with one stating 'Fig. 5 shows that this approach can be conducted at scale, providing a means of assessing the fitness of mutant pools.' The editor notes the authors 'show use of the strategy in a small-scale loss-of-function screen, providing compelling evidence that large-scale screens will be possible.' A reviewer confirms the authors 'validate this tool in a small-scale loss of function screen incorporating essential and non-essential genes, identifying the expected growth phenotypes.'

results.result: The authors demonstrate the utility of co-expressing AsCas12a ultra, T7 RNAP, and CBE for hybrid CRISPR gene replacement and base editing within the same cell line. They show that the introduction of a thymidine homo-polymer within the PF16 CDS produces the same motility phenotype observed when using gene replacement strategies for knockout generation. The ORF was successfully replaced by drug-resistance markers on both alleles, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and motility analysis revealed the expected PF16 motility phenotype.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this finding, with one noting 'Figs.1 and 4 demonstrate the capacity of the combined modifications to efficiently edit a gene in three different Leishmania species.' The editor describes the work as 'meticulously-developed' and reviewers raise no concerns about the hybrid approach or the validation experiments.

results.result: The authors developed a revised CBE sgRNA scoring system to prioritize STOP codon generation. A C-score was implemented that determines the ratio of available cytosines to resulting STOP codons. The new scoring system rates CBE sgRNAs higher when the STOP codon is introduced within positions 4–8 and lower when introduced within positions 11–12.
results.evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accept this improvement as part of the overall methodological advances. One reviewer notes the authors 'improve the sgRNA design' and predicts 'null mutants will be more efficiently produced after editing.' No concerns are raised about the scoring system.

results.result: All tested L. mexicana clones showed only unique sequencing reads, confirming the integration of only one guide per transfectant. However, for L. donovani and L. major, 2 out of 10 sequencing reads showed mixed guide sequences, suggesting that multiple CBE sgRNAs can be integrated per cell. The integration of multiple sgRNAs per cell remained random in L. donovani and L. major.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the overall characterization of the system. One reviewer notes the authors 'ensure that only a single sgRNA expression cassette integrates that edits with high efficiencies,' acknowledging the species-specific differences. No concerns are raised about the mixed integration in some species.

results.result: The authors conclude that these improvements will broaden the range of possible gene editing applications in Leishmania species and will enable a variety of loss-of-function screens in the near future. The improved toolbox sets the stage for various gene editing applications in Leishmania, including genome-wide CBE screens.
results.evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this conclusion. The editor states the work provides 'compelling evidence that large-scale screens will be possible' and that 'The newly developed tools will be of great interest to researchers working with Leishmania and beyond.' A reviewer confirms 'The combination of these two improvements should open the door to exciting large-scale screens' and 'we have no doubt that the technology established here, will be very useful for the Leishmania research community and beyond.'

comparisons.comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C10, C113-C114) regarding the improved sgRNA scoring system. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of validation data ('will be systematically tested in future studies'), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the improvement as part of overall methodological advances without raising concerns about validation.

Perfect claim overlap (C23, C115-C118) on the hybrid gene replacement approach. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes it's a proof-of-concept rather than extensive validation, while peer reviewers affirm the demonstration across three Leishmania species without concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C24-C25, C129) on forward-looking impact statements. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges these are speculative but reasonable given demonstrated improvements, while peer reviewers strongly endorse the potential for large-scale screens and utility to the research community.

High claim overlap (87.5% Jaccard) on T7 RNAP promoter optimization (C9, C48-C53). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative improvements (7 vs 33 days, no growth defects), while peer reviewers highlight reduced toxicity and retained editing efficiency as part of the meticulously-developed strategy.

Strong claim overlap (57.7% Jaccard) on pooled screen results (C13-C22, C97-C112). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation (24 targeting sgRNAs, 15 controls, ~25,000 cells/sgRNA), while peer reviewers confirm the small-scale loss-of-function screen successfully identified expected growth phenotypes.

Moderate claim overlap (50% Jaccard) on Cas12a integration system (C59-C69). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details the ~25-fold improvement and independence from homology flank length, while peer reviewers emphasize the 400-fold transfection efficiency improvement and compelling documentation of AsCas12a usefulness.

Partial claim overlap (27.3% Jaccard) on combined CBE-Cas12a system (C11, C72-C76). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the 400-fold transfection efficiency improvement (1/70 cells) and complete tdTomato depletion, while peer reviewers confirm the efficiency improvement and integration usefulness across multiple figures.

Minimal claim overlap (C12 only) on the key transfection efficiency metric. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this as a standalone quantitative achievement (400-fold improvement to 1/70 cells), while peer reviewers incorporate it into broader validation of the Cas12a integration approach.

Partial claim overlap (35.3% Jaccard) on PF16 targeting experiments (C81-C84, C86-C87). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details rapid editing (6 days) and notes the L. mexicana reversal with growth defect, while peer reviewers affirm efficient editing across three Leishmania species without raising concerns.

Partial claim overlap (37.5% Jaccard) on integration patterns (C94-C96). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes species differences in integration (single-copy in L. mexicana vs. multiple guides in some L. donovani/L. major clones), while peer reviewers accept this as ensuring single sgRNA cassette integration with high efficiency.

Partial claim overlap (29.4% Jaccard) on integration characterization (C88-C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed sequencing validation (ONT/Illumina, read coverage analysis), while peer reviewers accept the overall editing capacity across species as part of the meticulously-developed strategy.

Minor claim overlap (14.3% Jaccard) on combined system results (C70-C71, C78). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on tdTomato depletion and library representation calculations, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall editing efficiency across three Leishmania species.

OpenEval evaluates background/motivation claims (C1-C3, C26-C36, C119-C126) as SUPPORTED, establishing biological and technical challenges with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory context claims.

OpenEval evaluates prior CBE system description and limitations (C4-C8, C37-C47) as SUPPORTED, all citing Engstler and Beneke 2023. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these baseline comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates trade-offs of dual-construct system (C127-C128) as SUPPORTED, noting both disadvantages (requiring stable cell line) and advantages (efficient integration). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this balanced assessment.
